title: PixelForge run manifest
description: Describes one batch bake: the sheets written, the animation layout needed to read them, and the skin ramps they were recoloured into. This file is the shipped contract — consumers read it, PixelForge only writes it. Validate against the copy of this schema that shipped in the SAME export folder, never a pinned or vendored one: most objects here deliberately permit additional properties so that a later minor version can add an optional field without breaking you, and a pinned copy gives up that protection for no gain, since the matching schema always travels with the artifacts. The three objects that do forbid extra properties (slots, curatedClip.rows, fullLayout.facingRows) each say why in their own description.

$schema.description: Relative path to the schema copied beside this manifest, so an editor validates it with no network access.

schemaVersion.description: Semantic version of this manifest format, and the single place it is declared — the writer emits this constant rather than a literal of its own, so a drifted producer fails validation instead of shipping a plausible but wrong version. Policy: an optional property added at one of the open objects below is a MINOR bump. A change to one of the three closed objects (slots, curatedClip.rows, fullLayout.facingRows), or a removed, retyped or newly required property anywhere, mints a new $id, a new -vN filename and a new generated type.

runId.description: UUIDv7 identifying the bake run. Leads with a millisecond timestamp, so run ids sort chronologically.

sheets.description: Every sheet the run wrote, in bake order.

hexColor.description: Opaque RGB colour, uppercase hex. Alpha is never carried — the recolour only ever substitutes opaque pixels.

facing.description: Direction the avatar faces. Curated sheets drop north entirely.

name.description: Identity of the ramp. Names are unique case-insensitively; a custom ramp may not shadow a built-in.

isHuman.description: Whether this reads as human skin. Fantasy tones are reachable only by explicit choice, never by a hashed default.

steps.description: The five ramp steps, darkest shadow first. Index 3 is the base tone — what a viewer thinks of as 'the' colour of this ramp.

palette.description: The colours behind the run. A recolour is a straight index-for-index substitution of five colours — no blending, no dithering, no colour-space maths.

sourceRamp.description: The ramp every source partial is authored in, and therefore what each sheet's tone was substituted FROM.

ramps.description: The distinct tones this run actually substituted INTO, including any custom ramps. A run that applied no tone carries an empty array.

frameCount.description: Frames in this clip. They occupy output columns 0 to frameCount-1 of the clip's row; trailing cells up to the sheet's column count are transparent.

sourceColumn.description: Provenance only: the column of frame 0 in the 23-column source sheet. NOT an output column — curated frames are always left-aligned from column 0.

rows.description: Output row this clip occupies for each facing, stated per facing so a consumer never has to know the row formula. Closed to extra properties: the keys are the three facings curated geometry keeps, so an unrecognised key is a producer bug, not a newer field. Adding north here would not be an addition — curated geometry drops it deliberately.

columns.description: Source columns to draw, in playback order. This repeats and descends — walk is 1, 2, 1, 0 — so it MUST NOT be re-sorted or de-duplicated.

isRenderedByDefault.description: Whether the generator treats this clip as a playable animation rather than a single pose.

reverseDrawOrder.description: Whether this clip composites in the generator's alternate layer ordering. True for climb alone. This is NOT a back-to-front reversal of the normal order, and implementing it by reversing the layer array renders the clip wrong. The normal order is shadow, backExtra, backHair, bottom, top, head, hair, frontExtra, hat, weapon; the alternate order is shadow, weapon, frontExtra, bottom, top, head, hair, backExtra, backHair, hat. The body core -- bottom, top, head, hair -- is IDENTICAL in both. Only the back/front accessory pairs swap, which is what a character seen from behind requires: what was behind comes forward.

curatedLayout.description: The curated sheet: 8 clips on 3 facings, north dropped, frames left-aligned per row.

columns.description: Columns in the sheet, set by the widest clip.

rows.description: Rows in the sheet: one per clip per facing.

frameDurationMs.description: How long each frame is held. The deliberate cadence of this art style — play at this rate rather than guessing.

facings.description: Facings this geometry carries, in row order within a clip.

fullLayout.description: The raw source assembly, written without a remap: all source columns on all four facing rows.

facingRows.description: Sheet row each facing occupies. Fixed for every clip in this geometry, which is why it sits on the layout rather than on each clip. Closed to extra properties: the keys are the four source facings, a complete enumeration, so an unrecognised key is a producer bug rather than a newer field.

layouts.description: A layout appears only when the run actually produced that geometry, so a manifest never describes files that are not in the folder.

slots.description: The partial that filled each layer slot, back to front, by stem. A slot the sheet does not use is absent rather than empty. Closed to extra properties: the keys are the ten character layers the generator composites, a complete enumeration, so an unrecognised key is a misspelled slot rather than a newer field. A new slot here is a breaking change by definition — it would alter the draw order.

file.description: The file written, including extension. Lossless WebP, verified by round trip.

geometry.description: Which layout under layouts describes this sheet.

tone.description: Name of the ramp under palette.ramps this sheet's skin was substituted into. Absent when the sheet carries no skin and keeps its authored colours.

hero.description: The hero directory this sheet belongs to, such as villager_01. Present on a hero's base body sheet; ABSENT on a standalone attachment layer, which belongs to no hero and is shared by all of them. There is deliberately no ordering property here: a consumer stacks layers by the fixed order given in fullClip.reverseDrawOrder's description, which is constant across every curated clip and every facing, and each sheet names its own slot under slots.
